title: High-speed train collision near Toledo kills 69 in Spain
dek: A Renfe high-speed train ran into the back of a stationary Iryo train near Urda on 28 October, killing 69. Transport Minister Óscar Puente resigned on 3 November; a court and the rail accident board are investigating.
happened: At about 8:53 a.m. on 28 October, a Renfe AVE train travelling from Madrid to Seville struck the rear of an Iryo train that had stopped on the same line near Urda, in Toledo province. The two trains were carrying 544 people. The provisional death toll is 69; by 2 November forensic teams had identified 66 victims, 54 of them Spanish, and 41 people were still in hospital, 16 in intensive care.

sides.says: Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a fault in the main signalling system had stopped trains on that stretch and that the Atocha control centre then cleared the Renfe train to restart although a stop signal was still active; the controllers, he said, "had in plain sight what was happening". On 3 November he resigned, telling parliament a minister "cannot continue in office with two accidents of this severity in less than a year", and said he will not run in the coming election. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared three days of mourning and announced a €30 million aid package; bereaved families get €72,121 in direct aid plus the same again as advance compensation.

The PP, Vox, PNV and Junts had all demanded his resignation. The PP's Ester Muñoz said the minister's job "is not to explain fatal accidents, it is to prevent them". Vox's Pepa Millán said he was "shirking his responsibilities".

The 24-year-old controller who gave the restart order declined to answer the Civil Guard's questions; he is under formal investigation but not under arrest. The Adif operator regulating the line was also questioned. A court in Orgaz has opened an inquiry, and the accident board AITAT has recovered both trains' black boxes. Neither has reached conclusions on responsibility.

next: Three victims, believed to be foreign nationals, were still to be identified on 2 November. The Railway Safety Agency is reviewing the line's safety system and services on the Madrid-Seville line are reduced. The works council at the rail infrastructure operator Adif has agreed to push for a strike on 17 November, but none has been formally called. It is the second deadly crash this year, after a derailment in Andalusia in January killed 46 people. On 6 November Euronews reported that the European Public Prosecutor's Office has opened an investigation, on its own initiative, into possible fraud involving EU funds for renewing the line's safety, signalling and communications systems; the EU granted €111 million in 2024. The Transport Ministry opened applications for aid to victims on 6 November, until 5 February 2027. Spain holds a general election on 29 November.
summary: Spain is in mourning after a state-run Renfe high-speed train hit the back of a privately run Iryo train near Urda, in Toledo province, on the morning of 28 October. Both were travelling from Madrid towards Seville. The provisional death toll is 69, including four Americans, and 66 victims have been identified. The transport minister says a control centre cleared the Renfe train to move on despite an active stop signal; the controller is under formal investigation, and a court and the rail accident board are looking into the crash. Puente resigned on 3 November over the two deadly crashes this year. No one has yet been found responsible.
